Mesillat Yesharim 11:14: And the reasoning of the law dictates this, for stealing an object is theft, and stealing time is theft: just as one who steals an object and performs a mitzvah with it has his defender become his accuser, so too one who steals time and performs a mitzvah with it has his defender become his accuser.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:15: And the Holy One, blessed be He, desires nothing but faithfulness, as it is said (Psalms 31:24): "The Lord preserves the faithful." And it says (Isaiah 26:2): "Open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faith may enter in." And it says (Psalms 101:6): "My eyes are upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me." And it says (Jeremiah 5:3): "Are not Your eyes upon faithfulness?"
Mesillat Yesharim 11:16: And even Job testified concerning himself and said (Job 31:7): "If my step has turned out of the way, and my heart walked after my eyes, and if any blemish has cleaved to my hands." And observe the beauty of this metaphor, for he compared theft that is not revealed to something that clings to a person's hand — for even though the person does not set out at first to take it, and it merely remains clinging to him of itself, in the end it is nonetheless in his hand. So too with this matter: even though a person does not go about actually stealing, it is hard for his hands to remain entirely empty of it.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:17: However, in truth, all this results from the fact that instead of the heart ruling over the eyes, so as not to allow itself to find pleasing what belongs to others, the eyes draw the heart to seek out permissions for whatever appears to them beautiful and desirable. Therefore Job said that he did not do so, and his heart did not walk after his eyes; therefore no blemish clung to his hands.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:18: See now, in the matter of misrepresentation in business, how easy it is for a person to be enticed and to stumble, when it seems to him, at first glance, that it is proper for him to strive to make his merchandise appear beautiful in people's eyes and to profit by the labor of his hands, to speak persuasively to the buyer's heart so that he will be pleased with it, and people will say of all this, there is one who is alacritous and rewarded, and "the hand of the diligent makes rich."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:19: However, if he is not exacting and does not weigh his deeds carefully, then instead of wheat, thorns will come forth (cf. Job 31:40): for he will transgress the sin of misrepresentation, concerning which we were warned (Leviticus 25:14): "and you shall not wrong one another." And they said, of blessed memory (Chullin 94a): even to deceive a non-Jew is forbidden, and Scripture says explicitly (Zephaniah 3:13): "The remnant of Israel shall do no wrong, and shall not speak lies, neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:20: And so they said (Bava Metzia 60a): one may not touch up old vessels to make them appear new.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:21: One may not mix produce with produce, even new with new, even a se'ah's worth with a dinar's worth. And even if a dinar's worth and a smaller unit's worth are both fine, one should not mix them and sell them at the se'ah-for-a-dinar rate. Anyone who does these things is "anyone who does injustice" (Deuteronomy 25:16), and is called by five names: unjust, hated, loathsome, abominated, an abomination.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:22: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bava Kamma 119a): whoever steals from his fellow even the worth of a perutah is regarded as though he had taken his life from him. Behold, then, the gravity of this sin even in a very small amount. And they further said (Ta'anit 7b): rain is withheld only because of the sin of theft. And they further said (Vayikra Rabbah 33): a basket full of sins — which one accuses first among them all? Theft. And the generation of the Flood had its sentence sealed only because of theft (Sanhedrin 108a).
Mesillat Yesharim 11:23: And should you say in your heart: how is it possible for us not to strive, in our business dealings, to persuade our fellow regarding the merchandise and its value?
Mesillat Yesharim 11:24: There is a great distinction in the matter: whatever is done to show buyers the true goodness and beauty of the item — such an effort is good and proper. But whatever is done to conceal the flaws of one's merchandise is nothing but misrepresentation and is forbidden. This is a great principle in the honesty required in business dealings.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:25: I will not even speak of the matter of weights and measures, for concerning them it is written explicitly: "an abomination to the Lord your God is anyone who does these things." And they said, of blessed memory (Bava Batra 88b): the punishment for dishonest measures is more severe than the punishment for sexual immorality, etc. And they said (ibid.): a wholesale grain-dealer must wipe clean his measures once every thirty days. And why all this? So that they will not become deficient unknowingly, and he will not be punished.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:26: All the more so the sin of usury, which is grave — like one who denies the God of Israel, God forbid (Bava Metzia 71a). And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shemot Rabbah 31) on the verse: "he has given forth upon usury, and has taken increase; shall he then live? He shall not live" (Ezekiel 18:13) — that he will not live to see the resurrection of the dead, for he and even its dust are loathsome and abominable in the eyes of the Lord. And I see no need to elaborate on this, for its dread already weighs upon every man of Israel.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:27: However, the general rule of the matter is: just as the desire for money is great, so its pitfalls are many. And in order for a person to become truly clean of them, he needs great reflection and much exactitude. And if he becomes clean of it, let him know that he has already attained a great level,
Mesillat Yesharim 11:28: for many practice piety in many branches of piety, but in the matter of hatred of unjust gain they have been unable to reach the destination of perfection. This is what Tzofar the Naamathite said to Job (Job 11:14): "If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away, and let not wrongdoing dwell in your tents; for then shall you lift up your face without blemish; yes, you shall be steadfast, and shall not fear."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:29: Now, I have spoken thus far of the particulars of a single commandment, and of these kinds of distinctions; and certainly such particulars can be found in every single commandment. However, I mention only those in which most people are commonly prone to stumble.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:30: Let us now speak of sexual immorality, which is likewise among the grave transgressions, and is second in rank to theft, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said, in these words (Bava Batra 165a): "The majority sin in theft, and a minority in sexual immorality."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:31: Now, whoever wishes to become entirely cleansed of this sin will also need no small labor. For the prohibition includes not only the act itself, but everything close to it. And Scripture says explicitly (Leviticus 18:6): "None of you shall approach to uncover nakedness."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:32: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shemot Rabbah 16): The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Do not say, since it is forbidden to me to have relations with this woman, I will hold her and incur no sin, I will embrace her and incur no sin, or I will kiss her and incur no sin. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: just as if a Nazirite vowed not to drink wine, it is forbidden for him to eat fresh or dried grapes, grape residue, and anything that comes from the grapevine, so too a woman who is not yours — it is forbidden to touch her at all. And whoever touches a woman who is not his brings death upon himself, etc.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:33: And observe how wondrous the words of this statement are, for it compares this prohibition to that of the Nazirite, who, even though the essential prohibition is only the drinking of wine, the Torah forbade him everything connected with wine. And this was a lesson the Torah taught the Sages, how they should make a fence for the Torah in the safeguard entrusted to them, to make for its own protection.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:34: For they should learn from the Nazirite to forbid, for the sake of the essential prohibition, also everything resembling it. It follows that the Torah did, in this commandment of the Nazirite, what it entrusted to the Sages to do for all the other commandments — so that it be known that this is the will of the Omnipresent; and when He forbids us one of the prohibitions, the unstated is to be learned from the explicit, to forbid everything close to it.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:35: And in this manner they forbade, regarding this matter of sexual immorality, everything of the same kind as illicit relations, or close to it, in whatever sense it may be — that is, whether in deed, in sight, in speech, in hearing, and even in thought. And now I will bring you proofs for all these from the words of our Sages, of blessed memory.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:36: In deed — that is, touching or embracing and the like — has already been explained above in the statement we mentioned, and there is no need to elaborate.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:37: In sight — our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot): "hand to hand, the evil man shall not go unpunished" (Proverbs 11:21) — whoever counts out money from his hand into her hand in order to gaze at her will not be acquitted of the judgment of Gehinnom. And they further said (Shabbat 64a): why did Israel of that generation need atonement? Because their eyes feasted on illicit sights, etc. Rav Sheshet said: why did Scripture list outer ornaments together with inner ornaments? To tell you that whoever gazes at a woman's small finger is as though he gazed at the place of her nakedness (Berachot 24a).
Mesillat Yesharim 11:38: And they further said: "and you shall guard yourself from every evil thing" (Deuteronomy 23:10) — that a person should not gaze at a beautiful woman, even if she is unmarried; at a married woman, even if she is unattractive (Avodah Zarah 20a).
Mesillat Yesharim 11:39: Regarding conversing with a woman, we learned explicitly (Avot 1:5): whoever converses excessively with a woman brings evil upon himself.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:40: And regarding hearing, they said (Berachot 24a): a woman's voice is nakedness.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:41: Further, regarding the immorality of the mouth and the ear — that is, speaking words of lewdness or listening to such things — they have already cried out like a crane and said (Yerushalmi Terumot 1): "and there shall be seen in you no unseemly thing" (Deuteronomy 23:15) — this refers to unseemly speech, that is, foul language.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:42: And they said (Shabbat 33a): because of the sin of foul language, troubles are renewed, and the young men of Israel's enemies die.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:43: And they further said (ibid.): whoever speaks foul language — Gehinnom is deepened for him.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:44: And they further said (ibid.): everyone knows why a bride enters the bridal canopy; nevertheless, whoever speaks obscenely about it, etc. — even a sentence of seventy years for good is turned to evil for him.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:45: And they further said (Chagigah 5b): even a light conversation between a man and his wife is declared to a person at the time of judgment.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:46: And regarding listening to such evil speech, they also said (Shabbat 33a): even one who hears and remains silent is culpable, as it is said (Proverbs 22:14): "he who is cursed by the Lord shall fall there."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:47: Behold, then, that all the senses must be clean of illicit matters and their content.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:48: And if someone should whisper to you, saying that what they said about foul language is only meant to intimidate and keep a person far from transgression, and that these words apply only to one whose blood runs hot, for whom speaking of such things leads to actual desire — but one who says it merely in jest has done nothing, and there is no need to be concerned about him —
Mesillat Yesharim 11:49: you should answer him: this is nothing but the words of the evil inclination. For it is a complete verse that our Sages, of blessed memory, brought as their proof (Isaiah 9:16): "Therefore the Lord shall have no joy in their young men, etc., for everyone is a hypocrite and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks folly." Behold, this verse mentions neither idolatry, nor sexual immorality itself, nor bloodshed, but rather hypocrisy, evil speech, and foul language — all sins of the mouth in speech — and concerning them the decree went out: "The Lord shall have no joy in their young men, and shall have no mercy on their orphans and widows."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:50: Rather, the truth is as our Sages, of blessed memory, say: that foul language is actually the "nakedness" of speech itself, and it is forbidden precisely because it is a form of illicit sexual matter, like all other matters of sexual immorality — except for the act itself; for even though there is no karet or capital punishment attached to them, they are forbidden in their own right, besides also being causes that lead to the primary prohibition itself. This is like the matter of the Nazirite mentioned in the Midrash we cited above.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:51: Regarding thought, they already said at the beginning of our baraita (Avodah Zarah 20b): "and you shall guard yourself from every evil thing" — that a person should not entertain improper thoughts by day, etc. And they further said (Yoma 29a): thoughts of transgression are more severe than the transgression itself. And Scripture says explicitly (Proverbs 15:26): "the thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to the Lord."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:52: Now, we have spoken of two grave categories of transgression, in whose branches people are prone to stumble, because of the great number of their branches and the great inclination of a person's heart toward them in his desire.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:53: And the third level, after theft and sexual immorality, with regard to desire, is the prohibition of forbidden foods — whether regarding the non-kosher foods themselves, or regarding their admixtures, or regarding meat and milk, or forbidden fats and blood, and the matter of food cooked by non-Jews, and the matter of things repugnant prepared by non-Jews, their libation wine and ordinary wine. In all these, cleanliness requires great exactitude and requires strengthening, for there is the desire of the heart, which craves fine foods, and the loss to one's pocket in the prohibitions of admixtures, and the like.
